factNotes.interpretation: The band's sound experiments support a stylistic bridge into psychedelia. Keep this separate from its member-to-member links.

jazz-fusion.curatorFeedback: Keep jazz fusion attached to jazz while allowing documented rock, funk and progressive crossover. Do not pull every nearby jazz artist into rock.

eric-clapton.curatorFeedback: Connect the Yardbirds and Cream through verified membership, with blues guitar as the musical center. Hall of Fame inductions are career context, not new collaborations.

jimmy-page.curatorFeedback: Page links the Yardbirds' blues-rock lineage to Led Zeppelin's hard rock. His double-neck guitar is a separate instrument-use link, not a genre by itself.

factNotes.interpretation: This supports Page's use of a double-neck on stage. It explains an instrument connection, not a new musical genre.

led-zeppelin.curatorFeedback: Important overlap point between blues rock, classic rock and hard rock.

black-sabbath.curatorFeedback: Should behave as a bridge between hard rock, doom metal and heavy metal rather than sitting in a closed metal box.

the-yardbirds.curatorFeedback: Keep the band in British blues rock. Clapton, Beck and Page are documented former members whose later paths explain its wide bridge role; membership does not imply a shared later sound.

factNotes.interpretation: Use as evidence for separate membership links and a British blues-rock lineage. Do not infer simultaneous membership.
A pickup-switch specification enriches the guitar node only. Do not derive an artist or genre edge from hardware alone.

rickenbacker-360-12.curatorFeedback: The Harrison/Beatles recording use supports a concrete instrument-to-player bridge. A later artist being inspired to buy the model is influence context, not proof of a shared recording.

factNotes.interpretation: A documented player and recording context can bridge instrument and band. The guitar model remains in the workshop zone.

bluegrass.curatorFeedback: The genre name's link to Bill Monroe's band is an origin clue. Keep bluegrass rooted in early country and acoustic folk history, not modern pop-country.

factNotes.interpretation: This is a genre-origin relationship, not a claim that one person alone invented every part of the style.

jeff-beck.curatorFeedback: The Yardbirds are the documented roots link; later instrumental work gives Beck a separate jazz-fusion direction. Keep those reasons distinct.

steve-vai.curatorFeedback: Teaching, band work and guitar design are three different relationship types. Keep Vai close to Satriani, Zappa and the JEM for their documented reasons, not as one generic collaboration cluster.

factNotes.interpretation: Satriani taught Vai; Zappa later employed him. These are teaching and band/career relationships, not interchangeable collaboration edges.

joe-satriani.curatorFeedback: The documented Vai link is teacher-to-student. Keep it distinct from a shared recording or band-membership edge.

factNotes.interpretation: This records a Hall of Fame induction, not a joint performance or musical collaboration. Do not create a collaboration edge from it.

fender-esquire.curatorFeedback: The model belongs with Fender guitar history. Its documented use by Luther Perkins behind Johnny Cash gives it a specific country bridge; do not infer that Cash himself played this model.

factNotes.interpretation: The player was Luther Perkins, backing Johnny Cash. Keep Cash as scene context; do not claim Cash played the Esquire.

ramones.curatorFeedback: Major early punk anchor. Should help organize the punk-alt area and connect back to rock history.

misfits.curatorFeedback: Core punk and horror punk anchor. Keep near Ramones, Sex Pistols, horror punk and hardcore punk rather than generic rock.

sex-pistols.curatorFeedback: Major UK punk anchor. Should sit in the punk-alt core with clear relation to Ramones and early punk.

public-enemy.curatorFeedback: Hip-hop anchor with possible punk/rock crossover context. Keep hip-hop in its own area, but allow documented bridges.

g-funk.curatorFeedback: A funk sample or stylistic debt explains musical lineage. Keep G-funk in hip-hop; do not treat every funk influence as a direct artist-to-artist collaboration.

factNotes.interpretation: Use as a stylistic and production lineage inside hip-hop. Funk influence is not by itself a documented collaboration with a specific funk artist.

jimmie-rodgers.curatorFeedback: Keep Rodgers grounded in early country while letting his blues and early rock influence pull him toward those scenes.

the-carter-family.curatorFeedback: The Carter Family is an early country anchor with documented folk and blues repertoire.

merle-haggard.curatorFeedback: Haggard belongs in country while his documented jazz and blues influences make him a useful bridge.

rules.feedback: Zones are guidance, not cages. Strong bridge nodes may bleed outside the visual rectangle when it improves readability.
Wikipedia categories are weak signals. Do not create or prioritize category-like genre nodes unless they are recognized music genres.
Songs, albums and releases can explain a connection, but should not become graph nodes.

Never allow the map to become visually unreadable. Dense clusters are acceptable when they feel like organized chaos, but labels must not overlap heavily, node labels must remain readable, and important names should not stack on top of each other. If a zone becomes too crowded, expand the local layout, increase spacing, or let bridge nodes drift outward instead of compressing everything into one tight cluster.

feedbackCategories.label: Too dense
feedbackCategories.feedback: A local cluster is too compressed. Nodes may sit close together, but labels must remain readable and important names must not stack.

feedbackCategories.label: Label overlap
feedbackCategories.feedback: Visible labels collide or form unreadable piles. The renderer should hide lower-priority labels when zoomed out, and layout should increase spacing.

feedbackCategories.label: Wrong zone
feedbackCategories.feedback: A node is placed in a zone that does not match its strongest music-history context.

feedbackCategories.label: Good bridge
feedbackCategories.feedback: A node usefully connects two or more zones. Preserve its cross-zone pull instead of forcing it into a sealed cluster.

feedbackCategories.label: Bad node type
feedbackCategories.feedback: A candidate is not one of the allowed visible map node types: band, guitarist, artist, guitar, guitar_brand or genre.

feedbackCategories.label: Genre transition needed
feedbackCategories.feedback: Neighboring scenes need more documented bridge nodes so the map reads like a music-history flow, not separate boxes.

feedbackCategories.label: Category grouping
feedbackCategories.feedback: Category-like labels such as duos, groups, people, artists, albums or companies are not concrete music genres and should not become visible nodes.

feedbackCategories.label: Platform or reference
feedbackCategories.feedback: Music platforms, magazines, databases, institutions and reference works are source context, not visible map nodes.

bridgePolicies.feedback: The rock to hard-rock/metal path should overlap strongly. Let bridge nodes drift between zones rather than forming a straight, sterile lane.
